source_of_truth: backend/src/modules/import/{import.validate.js, import.service.js, import.parse.js} (working tree, post Wave A/B/C of docs/import-ux-study/03-TRIAGE-MATRIX.md)
description: Machine-readable catalog of every import_batch_errors.error_code an operator can see from the bulk-import pipeline, keyed for future i18n/frontend consumption. Companion human-readable doc: docs/import-guide/ERROR_GLOSSARY.md (same data, prose form). Excludes __INVALID_PARENT__ (internal sentinel row, filtered out of every operator-facing response by import.service.js before it ever reaches a batch's visible error list or getBatchDetail) and the no-code upload/confirm HTTP-level rejection messages (see ERROR_GLOSSARY.md's appendix — those never get an error_code or an import_batch_errors row at all).
ordering: codes[] is grouped by stage_group in the order listed in stage_group_order, and alphabetical by code within each group. This ordering is stable across regenerations as long as the code list itself doesn't change.

severity_value_notes.null: This code is never emitted in this mode at all (e.g. IO_AUTO_PROVISIONED only ever fires for legacy imports; IO_NOT_REGISTERED covers the equivalent non-legacy case instead).

keystone_fields._comment: Mirrors import.validate.js's KEYSTONE_FIELDS + OR_GROUP_KEYSTONES exactly. REQUIRED_MISSING findings on these field_keys are ERROR in BOTH severity_legacy and severity_nonlegacy, overriding the general legacy-mode WARNING demotion described on REQUIRED_MISSING below. Independent of this table: RECORD_DATE_MISSING, PS_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_IN_DB, IO_NOT_REGISTERED, PARENT_KEY_BLANK/UNMATCHED, and DUPLICATE_IN_SHEET are their own dedicated codes, already ERROR-in-both-modes by design — they are not part of this field-level table.

codes.message_template: Duplicate {code_label} "{value}" found in sheet "{sheet_name}".
codes.operator_action: Check the two rows sharing this FIR/GD Number — delete the genuine duplicate, or correct whichever row has the wrong number typed in.

codes.message_template: Fill the "{parent_key_field}" column on sheet '{sheet_name}' — it must repeat the parent row's {parent_key_field} so this row can be linked.
codes.operator_action: Type the same FIR Number / GD Number into this row as appears on its General Information row.
codes.notes: Does not fire when the file has exactly one General Information row — see PARENT_KEY_RECOVERED instead.

codes.message_template: Blank "{parent_key_field}" in sheet '{sheet_name}' was auto-linked to this file's only parent row — verify this is correct.
codes.operator_action: No action required. Confirm the linked row actually belongs to the file's one case/arrest/GD.
codes.notes: Only fires when the parent sheet has exactly one row (never positional inference, never for the multi-parent case).

codes.message_template: Reference '{value}' in sheet '{sheet_name}' does not match any row in the parent sheet — check for a typo, or a missing parent row.
codes.operator_action: Check the value for a typo against the General Information sheet, or confirm the parent row exists there at all.

codes.severity_legacy_note: Overridden to ERROR when field_key is one of this record type's keystone fields (see the top-level keystone_fields table) — not a plain per-code severity, it depends on which field is missing.
codes.message_template: "{field_label}" is required in sheet "{sheet_name}".

message_variants.template: Either "Date Missing Since" or "GD Date" is required for a Missing Person record.

message_variants.context: ARREST/KALANDRA — zero arrestee rows with a first name
message_variants.template: At least one Arrested Person (with First Name filled in) is required on the Person Arrested sheet.

codes.operator_action: If ERROR: fill in the named field before this row can import. If WARNING: the row already imported — fill in the field later via the interactive record screen when the information is available.

codes.message_template: FIR number "{fir_no}" already exists in the database for this Police Station.

message_variants.template: FIR number "{fir_no}" already exists in the database for this Police Station.

message_variants.context: confirm-time race backstop (23505 unique-violation caught and downgraded)
message_variants.template: This FIR was imported by a concurrent process between validation and confirmation.

codes.operator_action: Check whether the FIR was already entered by you or a colleague. If genuinely duplicate, remove the row. The confirm-time race variant means the row was NOT saved — re-import separately if still needed.
codes.notes: Only ever checked for CASE — arrest_details has no ps_id column and several arrestees legitimately share one FIR, so ARREST is never checked for this (by design, not a gap).

codes.message_template: District "{value}" does not match this batch's target district ("{target}").

message_variants.template: District "{value}" does not match this batch's target district ("{target}").
Police Station "{value}" does not match this batch's target station ("{target}").

codes.operator_action: Correct the District/Police Station cell on this row, or confirm the correct target station was selected for the whole batch before upload.

codes.message_template: No usable date found for this record (checked FIR/arrest/occurrence date fields).
codes.operator_action: Fill in at least one of the record's date columns with a valid dd-mm-yyyy date.

codes.message_template: IO with PIS number "{pis}" is not yet registered for this police station — it will be auto-registered from the sheet and needs SHO verification.
codes.operator_action: No action required to complete the import. Flag the auto-registered IO for SHO verification afterwards.
codes.notes: Legacy imports only — non-legacy imports use IO_NOT_REGISTERED (ERROR) for the same condition instead. Auto-provisioned IO row is matched globally by PIS (investigating_officers.pis_no has a global unique index, not PS-scoped) before creating a new one.

codes.message_template: No Investigating Officer information provided — the record will be saved without a linked IO; add one later via the interactive form.
codes.operator_action: No action required to complete the import. Link an IO later via the interactive record screen if the information becomes available.
codes.notes: Legacy imports only — fires when the io_pis cell is entirely blank.

codes.message_template: IO with PIS number "{pis}" is not registered for this police station. Register the IO first, then re-validate — or import now and this row will be skipped.
codes.operator_action: Register the IO at your station first and re-validate, or leave this row out of the import for now and add the IO later via the interactive form.
codes.notes: One of the few checks that is deliberately ERROR in both modes — no legacy leniency (D2, docs/import-ux-study/02-POLICY-DECISIONS.md). Legacy imports get IO_AUTO_PROVISIONED instead for the same underlying condition.

codes.message_template: Act "{act}" is not in the acts list — will be stored as free text.
codes.operator_action: No action required — the typed value is kept as free text. Double-check spelling if a known Act was intended.
codes.notes: Always WARNING regardless of legacy mode — this is informational (free-text acts are explicitly sanctioned by the schema's other_act_name column, same as the interactive form).

codes.message_template: Beat "{beat_no}" matched to a beat number in this station after normalizing — verify this is correct.
codes.operator_action: No action required — confirm the matched beat is the one intended.
codes.notes: Fires when a bare operator-typed number (e.g. "6") matches the leading digits of a beat_name at the batch's own target PS. PS-scoped only — no global bare-number matching (collision risk across stations).

codes.message_template: Local head "{local_head}" matched after normalizing punctuation/spacing — verify this is correct.
codes.operator_action: No action required — confirm the matched local head is correct.

codes.message_template: Major head "{major_head}" matched after normalizing punctuation/spacing — verify this is correct.
codes.operator_action: No action required — confirm the matched major head is correct.

codes.message_template: Minor head "{minor_head}" matched after normalizing punctuation/spacing — verify this is correct.
codes.operator_action: No action required — confirm the matched minor head is correct.

codes.message_template: Beat "{beat_no}" could not be matched.
codes.operator_action: Check the beat number with your station's records unit — the beat may genuinely not be in the reference data yet for this station.
codes.notes: In legacy mode the original typed value is preserved on the record (beat_raw, storage:extra) even though it couldn't be linked to a formal beat row.

codes.message_template: Local head "{local_head}" could not be matched.
codes.operator_action: Check the spelling against the standard Local Head list.
codes.notes: In legacy mode the original typed value is preserved on the record (local_head_raw, storage:extra).

codes.message_template: Major head "{major_head}" could not be matched.
codes.operator_action: Check the spelling against the standard Major Head list.

codes.message_template: Minor head "{minor_head}" could not be matched.
codes.operator_action: Check the spelling, and confirm it belongs under the Major Head given on the same row.

codes.message_template: Section "{section}" (act "{act}") could not be matched to a known section.

message_variants.template: Section "{section}" (act "{act}") could not be matched to a known section.

message_variants.context: section given, no act text at all to resolve against
message_variants.template: Section "{section}" has no associated act to resolve against.

codes.operator_action: Check the Section number and its Act for typos; make sure the Act cell on the same row is filled in.

codes.message_template: Section "{section}" matched after normalizing zero-padding/spacing — verify this is correct.
codes.operator_action: No action required — confirm the matched section is correct.

codes.message_template: Missing required fields before submit: {field_label}, {field_label}, ...
codes.operator_action: No action required to complete the import (the record is saved as a draft). Fill in the listed fields via the interactive record screen before submitting it for review.
codes.notes: Never emitted for legacy imports (skipped entirely — legacy records land as LEGACY_IMPORTED and bypass workflow submission). Field labels are sourced from field_registry.labels.en at submit-validation time, not hardcoded here.

codes.message_template: Column "{column_label}" is informational and is not imported.
codes.operator_action: No action possible for this column's data — it is not a stored field. Record the information elsewhere if needed.
codes.notes: One warning per affected column per batch, never per row (row_number is always 0). Only fires for columns that carry a value AND are genuinely dropped (never for a column consumed elsewhere in the same bridge).

codes.message_template: Sheet "{sheet_name}": row(s) {row_numbers} appear empty/stray (1-2 filled cells, no key data) and were skipped.
codes.operator_action: No action required. If a listed row was meant to be real data, fill in its key fields and re-upload.
codes.notes: Parse-time skip (import.parse.js), surfaced as a validate-stage batch notice (row_number 0). Fires when a row has <=2 non-empty cells AND none of them is a keystone column for the record type.

codes.message_template: This file uses an older template version — please download the current template for future imports.
codes.operator_action: No action required for this batch — it imported using the older layout it matched. Download the current template before your next import.
codes.notes: Only fires for a KNOWN older layout (layout-manifests.js) that still scores above the acceptance threshold. A file matching no known layout at all is rejected outright before a batch is even created (UNKNOWN_LAYOUT_MESSAGE, no error_code — see ERROR_GLOSSARY.md appendix). PCR_CALL has no layout-manifest coverage and is never fingerprinted, so this code never fires for it.

codes.message_template: This row could not be saved due to a system error (ref: {batch_id}/{row_number}). Report this to your administrator.
codes.operator_action: Note the batch/row reference number shown and report it to your system administrator. Other rows in the batch are unaffected.
codes.notes: Deliberately sanitized — the real DB/JS error text is never shown to the operator (only written to the server log), by design (T7.2, docs/import-ux-study/03-TRIAGE-MATRIX.md). Only fires for a row that passed every validate-stage check but still violates a DB constraint the validator doesn't replicate (a known un-mitigated case: gender/relation_type/property-status CHECK vocabulary mismatches, see docs/import-ux-study/VALIDATION_INVENTORY.md F7). A 23505 unique-violation on fir_details is caught separately and downgraded to DUPLICATE_IN_DB (WARNING) instead of reaching this code.
